findings.finding: diagnosticLog calls log, append, and read/write. Those functions use WScript.Echo and ADODB.Stream; none invokes fileHash, freshHashSet, launchCertutil, shell.Exec, or shell.Run.
lockSnapshotAt reads the owner metadata and computes its generation with textHash, the embedded JavaScript SHA256 implementation. No external certificate/hash process is launched.
No writeOwner function exists in the current runner or follower. acquireRunnerLock writes owner.txt through write; releaseRunnerLock checks text through lockSnapshot.

After existing workers drain, parallelAssertShutdownInventory rechecks owner metadata, owned process handles, WMI inventory, and the original worker guard. Retry logging and sleeping do not create hashes. Two in-memory observations show zero tool launches on these paths.

parallelShutdownInventory removes an exact, same-owner preadmitted relative-script host. Its children remain in the guarded inventory. An unreadable relevant child causes a tagged retry even when its parent is the admitted host.

A new unreadable child in each of six snapshots can retain the lock without a single long-lived child. Increasing a retry count alone cannot guarantee resolution while a separate host continues creating such rows.

The entry-point message after parallelShutdown=false says owned workers remain live or uncertain even when the owned-handle list drained and the failure is an unclassified external inventory row. Diagnostic wording should preserve that distinction.

future_focused_test_matrix.expectation: Simulate six changing certutil PIDs under the same admitted host. Any newly allowed outcome must cite additional observed identity/workspace/exit evidence or an explicit revised policy; do not silently label them unrelated.
A readable command referencing the current absolute workspace remains guarded regardless of parent, prior admission, or executable name.
Parent/child PID reuse, changed CreationDate, changed host command, unreadable parent identity, or owner replacement cannot inherit an exception for a different identity.
An unreadable process outside the narrowly justified relation remains uncertain. A newly visible blocker must not be hidden because a previous PID disappeared.
Live or unknown retained Lean/RAM process handles still block release. A handle becoming live/unknown across an inventory boundary cannot be ignored.
WMI/query/read errors retain uncertainty; any retry has a documented finite scheduled-sleep/attempt budget without assuming a WMI wall-clock bound.
Fresh-current-owner shutdown handling must not silently relax stale or legacy lock reclamation.
Logging, owner validation, and a successful/failed shutdown inventory launch no new hash/compiler/helper process.
A cleanup failure may retain separately recorded successful audit-stage evidence, but never fabricate runtime success, receipt content, module compilation, or mathematical closure.

limits: No source edits made by this review.
No native Windows, real WSH/WMI, Lean/Lake, C#, Wine or CI execution.
Baseline synthetic parent and process rows model the reported structure only; they do not determine real native command lines or workspace ownership.
No final repair design or candidate implementation was available when this review was written.
